metadata.licensingAgency: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration
metadata.sourceManual: Maryland Driver's Manual, committed at src/assets/drivers-manuals/MD.pdf. Citations name the manual's printed page, which is also its physical page. The previous corpus was built from the open web before the manual was kept locally: 164 of its 221 laws carried no citation at all and 22 pointed at practice-test vendors. This one is built from the manual and nothing else.

knowledgeTest.passMarkBasis: Not in the manual: printed 7 gives the question count and the time limit -- 'There are 25 questions on the test. You will have 20 minutes to take the test.' -- and 56 pages state no pass mark anywhere. The 22 was inherited from the pre-rebuild corpus and was unsupported until 2026-09-07, when the MVA's own knowledge-test page was read and states it: 'You must score 88% or higher to pass'. 88% of 25 is 22. Sourced to the agency rather than to the book, which is the one exception how-to-build-laws.md allows for the exam's shape. The MVA page is now archived beside the manual as MD-exam.html, retrieved 2026-09-22 and pinned by sha256 under examSource in SOURCES.json, and it still states both figures: 'Class C, Class M, and Moped Permit: 25 questions' and 'You must score 88% or higher to pass'. From 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-22 this field named that page and nothing held the page's bytes, which is the failure manual-first-law-sourcing.md describes for laws. shapeCitations below is what holds this corpus to those sentences.

shapeCitations.quote: There are 25 questions on the test.
Class C, Class M, and Moped Permit: 25 questions
You must score 88% or higher to pass

knowledgeTest.languagesBasis: Not in the manual either: printed 12 lists the accommodations the MVA offers -- sign language, oral testing, screen readers, extra time -- and gives no count of languages. The 17 was inherited from the pre-rebuild corpus and was unsupported until 2026-09-07, when the MVA's knowledge-test page was read and names them all: English, Spanish, American Sign Language, Amharic, Arabic, Chinese (Traditional), Farsi, French, Hindi, Korean, Nepali, Portuguese, Russian, Tagalog, Urdu, Vietnamese, Yoruba. Seventeen, counted. It describes the MVA's paper and never this app, which is written in English only.

conceptModel.rationale: Every law traces to a page of the Maryland Driver's Manual. The pool is far larger than the 25-question paper so repeat runs differ, and it is not narrowed to predicted questions -- narrowing destroys the predictive validity the app exists to provide.

signImagery.expanded: Sign-recognition questions are 17% of the pool. The manual carries an explicit color and shape table, which is where the signs-by-description concept comes from. Twelve signs-by-picture laws (MD-205 to MD-216) ask the reverse -- the sign named in words, the learner picks one of four pictures -- which is the format the MVA's own knowledge test uses. They sit outside the pictorial concepts and carry no `sign` of their own; each of their answers does. The share above counts laws that show a sign, so they are not in it.

factCheck.scope: Built from the manual rather than checked against it afterwards: all 216 laws carry a citation naming the printed page that supports them. Every quote was matched against the text of the page it names, and every sign law was checked by rendering the page and the artwork side by side -- both by hand, on 2026-09-07, with no committed script to re-run them. What the suite re-checks is narrower: that the PDF is present, that its sha256 matches, and that no citation names a page past the end.
factCheck.notChecked: The committed PDF is the only authority used. The previous corpus stated eleven figures that appear nowhere in it -- the 0.07 DWI threshold, a $570 school-bus fine, the 1967 seat-belt requirement, a 55 mph default speed limit. All are real Maryland law and none is in the book a learner is told to study, so none of them is taught here. This manual contains no statutory speed limit table at all.

laws.law: The sign that warns of two roads merging is a warning sign, which gives notice of a situation that might not be readily apparent.
laws.why: Merging traffic arrives from the side you are not looking at, which is why the warning comes first.
laws.question: Which of these signs warns of two roads merging?

answers.answer: The two-roads-merging sign
The road-divides-ahead sign
The lane-ends sign
The signal-ahead sign

laws.law: The sign that warns the road is slippery when wet is a warning sign, which gives notice of a situation that might not be readily apparent.
laws.why: The road looks the same wet or dry; the sign is how you know before the car tells you.
laws.question: Which of these signs warns that the road is slippery when wet?

laws.law: The round railroad warning sign is used to warn that there is a railroad crossing ahead.
laws.why: The train cannot stop for you, so the warning has to reach you well before the tracks.
laws.question: Which of these signs warns of a railroad crossing ahead?

answers.answer: The railroad-warning sign
The crossbuck
The school-zone sign
The no-passing-zone sign

citations.location: p.20 (printed) — 'Round: Railroad Warning Used to warn that there is a railroad crossing ahead.'

laws.law: The five-sided pentagon shape warns you of school zones and marks school crossings.
laws.why: Children step off a curb without looking; the shape tells you to be the one who is looking.
laws.question: Which of these signs warns of a school zone or school crossing?

answers.answer: The school-zone sign
The no-passing-zone sign
The wildlife-crossing sign
The railroad-warning sign
